question: What practical approach does Casey Winters recommend for interviewing product managers?
expected_points: Use realistic scenarios drawn from the role rather than relying on rehearsed answers or work-history questions.
Assess whether candidates can suggest reasonable ideas and figure out how to test them quickly.
Use prompts or presentations to see candidates demonstrate the actual job.
evidence_quote: I'm going to give you real scenarios that I expect from the role. I want to hear how you'd approach them.

answer.summary: Casey Winters recommends assessing PM candidates through realistic job scenarios rather than rehearsed answers, looking for practical ideas, quick ways to test them, sound timing and metrics judgment, and whether they enjoy the work.

sections.heading: Use realistic work scenarios
sections.content: He says he does not focus on work history or polished “tell me about a time” answers. Instead, give candidates scenarios they can expect in the role and ask how they would approach them. Look for a few reasonable ideas and a way to test them quickly without analyst support or research. A presentation or prompt can help show how they would do the actual job—and whether they seem to enjoy it.

sections.heading: Watch for judgment red flags
sections.content: Pay attention if a candidate proposes solutions that would take months of engineering work to produce a signal, fails to account for how long a solution will take, or does not distinguish metrics expected to improve from metrics to track as safeguards. Winters calls interviewing an imperfect, “lossy” format, so this approach is not a guarantee of success.
